name: Lucas Cranach the Elder
findings: Uses smoky black 2.6x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 832 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, tumbleweed turns up as a small accent in 54% of the paintings that hold it, 3.9x the archive's rate (from 832 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, antique green turns up as the lightest note in 80% of the paintings that hold it, 7.5x the archive's rate (from 832 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, umber brown turns up as the shadow in 100% of the paintings that hold it, 1.8x the archive's rate (from 832 paintings here).
Pairs falu red with persian plum more than chance would predict (3 of 832 paintings here).
Pairs serpentine green with spanish bistre more than chance would predict (3 of 832 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, black, raisin black) covers 53% of his paintings here.
Keeps 2 distinct palette families here, from smoky black, black to smoky black, dark olive brown.
